why: import-boundary is a denylist of rival packages, and four lint cycles in a row found a new ring of them: lint-4.6, lint-5.4, lint-6.7 (19 packages) and lint-7.5 (6 of 22: antd, HeroUI, RTK Query, classnames, Material React Table, reconnecting-websocket). lint-6.7 and the v3-lint-6-lint brief named a fourth ring as the point where a different design, an allow list of the stack's packages per category, is worth a Spec. Each ring costs a cycle to find and a fix row to add, and an agent who reaches for a kit the list has not met yet is told nothing.
what: A one-page Spec on how import-boundary should decide what is a rival package, then the change it settles on.
change: Spec first (checkpoint `spec`): measure the denylist against the package names in the fixtures of lint cycles 1 to 7 and in the playground's and the examples' `package.json`; state the options with their cost: (a) keep the denylist and grow it per cycle; (b) an allow list per category (UI primitives, charts, data and routing, persistence, markdown, toasts, command palette, tables, class composition), where an import that is not the stack's and matches a category's signature (the package's name pattern, or a known component export) reports; (c) a manifest field naming the app's extra allowed packages beside either. Name the false-alarm risk of each against the playground, the examples and the 36 ejected primitives. Build the option the verdict picks.
commits: fix: or feat: one package commit for the form; the Spec is an artifact, not a commit.
proof: The lint cycle 7 harness (`docs/v3/cycles/lint-7/fixtures/run.sh`) reports every import-boundary seed of cycles 1 to 7 caught and every import `pass` mark silent; sweep.sh reports 0 import-boundary findings on the playground at `app` and `parts`.
acceptance: A Spec with the measured options and a default is submitted before the code it governs
Every import-boundary seed of lint cycles 1 to 7 is caught (seed report)
No import-boundary finding on the playground at `app` or `parts`, the 36 ejected primitives or the import `pass` marks (sweep, eject.sh, seed report)
out_of_scope: Rules other than import-boundary; rules for pinned 2.x consumers.
